extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers; mathematicians and computer scientists using GAP for computational algebra (partial permutations, semigroups, rings, modules)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference material describing definitions, properties, and GAP functions for partial permutations, partial-permutation semigroups, near-/additive magmas, and rings (including ideals) and their constructors/attributes. Useful for programmers using GAP to construct, inspect, and manipulate these algebraic objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShortLexLeqPartialPerm
rubrics_metrics.description: ShortLexLeqPartialPerm(f, g) returns true if the concatenation of the domain and image list of f is short-lex less than the corresponding concatenation for g and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that this is not the natural partial order on partial permutations nor the same as comparing f and g using <. Examples demonstrate that ShortLexLeqPartialPerm can give different results from the natural partial order and from the standard < comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrimPartialPerm
rubrics_metrics.description: TrimPartialPerm(f) changes the internal representation of a partial permutation f (e.g., from 32-bit to 16-bit integers) to use less memory when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operation modifies f in-place and returns nothing. Use when a composition causes the internal representation to use larger integer sizes than necessary (example showing IsPPerm4Rep before/after).

rubrics_metrics.name: PartialPermDisplayLimit
rubrics_metrics.description: PartialPermDisplayLimit is a user preference that determines when a partial permutation f of rank r is displayed in abbreviated form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rank r exceeds PartialPermDisplayLimit, f is displayed as: "<partial perm on r pts with degree m, codegree n>". Default value is 100. Example usage: SetUserPreference("PartialPermDisplayLimit", 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: NotationForPartialPerms - component
rubrics_metrics.description: NotationForPartialPerms = "component" displays partial permutations as products of disjoint permutations and chains: permutations shown like usual (fixed points in round brackets), chains in square brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A chain c is defined by: c[1] in domain but not image; c[i]^f = c[i+1] for i=1..n-1; c[n] in image but not domain. This is the default (most compact) notation. Example output: [1,3,14][16,8,2,12,15](4)(5,11)(19).

rubrics_metrics.name: NotationForPartialPerms - domainimage
rubrics_metrics.description: NotationForPartialPerms = "domainimage" displays f in the format: [ domain_list ] -> [ image_list ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corresponds to input of the form PartialPerm(DomainOfPartialPerm(f), ImageListOfPartialPerm(f)). It makes the domain and image explicit in two lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: NotationForPartialPerms - input
rubrics_metrics.description: NotationForPartialPerms = "input" displays f in the format PartialPerm([ domain_list ], [ image_list ]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matches the textual input representation (first type described in PartialPerm documentation) and is useful when you want an exact input-ready printout.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPartialPermSemigroup / IsPartialPermMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPartialPermSemigroup(obj) returns true iff obj satisfies IsSemigroup and IsPartialPermCollection. IsPartialPermMonoid(obj) returns true iff obj satisfies IsMonoid and IsPartialPermCollection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A partial perm semigroup may or may not be an inverse semigroup. Note: it is possible for a partial perm semigroup to have a multiplicative neutral element but not satisfy IsPartialPermMonoid in some contexts; when it does coincide, One(R) must match the multiplicative neutral element. See examples constructing semigroups with One(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeOfPartialPermSemigroup / Codegree / Rank
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeOfPartialPermSemigroup(S) is the largest degree of any partial permutation in S. CodegreeOfPartialPermSemigroup(S) is the largest positive integer appearing in the image of elements of S. RankOfPartialPermSemigroup(S) is the number of points on which S acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All return non-negative integers. Examples show using Semigroup(PartialPerm(...)) then querying Degree, Codegree, Rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricInverseSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: SymmetricInverseSemigroup(n) returns the inverse semigroup consisting of all partial permutations with degree and codegree at most n (n a non-negative integer). SymmetricInverseMonoid is a synonym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The symmetric inverse semigroup on n points has cardinality given by sum_{r=0}^n (n choose r)^2 r! (formula indicated in manual) and can be generated by a generating set for the symmetric group on n points plus any partial permutation of rank n-1. Example: S := SymmetricInverseSemigroup(5); Size(S) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSymmetricInverseSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSymmetricInverseSemigroup(S) returns true if the partial-perm semigroup S equals the symmetric inverse semigroup of degree n (where S has degree and codegree n), false otherwise. IsSymmetricInverseMonoid is a synonym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common terminology note: symmetric inverse monoid often referred to as symmetric inverse semigroup in literature. Examples show building S and testing property.

rubrics_metrics.name: NaturalPartialOrder / ReverseNaturalPartialOrder
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural partial order ≤ on an inverse semigroup S is defined by s ≤ t iff there exists an idempotent e in S with s = e t. For partial permutations, f ≤ g iff f is a restriction of g. NaturalPartialOrder(S) returns for each element i the set of positions of elements less than Elements(S)[i]; ReverseNaturalPartialOrder returns sets of positions greater than Elements(S)[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes return lists of sets of indices into Elements(S). See NaturalLeqPartialPerm for pairwise check; examples show NaturalPartialOrder(S) output and use in NaturalLeqPartialPerm(Elements(S)[i], Elements(S)[j]).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismPartialPermSemigroup / IsomorphismPartialPermMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismPartialPermSemigroup(S) / IsomorphismPartialPermMonoid(S) return an isomorphism from the inverse semigroup (or monoid) S to an inverse semigroup (or monoid) of partial permutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral notes: If S is a partial-perm semigroup that does not satisfy IsMonoid but MultiplicativeNeutralElement(S) <> fail, IsomorphismPartialPermMonoid returns an isomorphism to an inverse monoid of partial permutations. If S is a permutation group, the isomorphism uses AsPartialPerm and the inverse uses AsPermutation. If S is a transformation semigroup that is a monoid mathematically, an isomorphism to an inverse monoid of partial permutations is returned. Examples show creating iso and inspecting Range(iso).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNearAdditiveMagma
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNearAdditiveMagma(obj) denotes that obj is a near-additive magma: a domain A with an associative (not necessarily commutative) addition + : A × A → A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic additive category; many structures (modules, rings, fields) are additive magmas. See related categories for additional structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero(obj) denotes that obj is a near-additive magma with a zero (an additively neutral element z such that z + a = a = a + z for all a in A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero can be obtained using Zero(A) or Zero(a) or 0 * a. Note: a magma may contain an additive neutral element but not belong to the IsNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero category (see Section 31.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNearAdditiveGroup / IsNearAdditiveMagmaWithInverses
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNearAdditiveGroup(obj) (synonym IsNearAdditiveMagmaWithInverses) denotes a near-additive magma-with-zero A equipped with AdditiveInverse mapping -1*: A → A, giving additive inverses for elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition is assumed associative; this category gives closure under addition, zero, and additive inverses.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAdditiveMagma
rubrics_metrics.description: IsAdditiveMagma(obj) denotes that obj is an additive magma: a near-additive magma whose addition is commutative as well as associative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See IsAdditivelyCommutative for checking commutativity property.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAdditiveMagmaWithZero
rubrics_metrics.description: IsAdditiveMagmaWithZero(obj) denotes an additive magma that also has a zero element (unique additively neutral element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero can be computed with Zero(A) or Zero(a) or 0*a for any element a in A. A structure may contain a zero yet not be in this category.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAdditiveGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsAdditiveGroup(obj) (synonym IsAdditiveMagmaWithInverses) denotes an additive magma-with-zero that also provides additive inverses for each element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition is commutative and associative; this category provides closure under addition, zero, and additive inverses.

rubrics_metrics.name: NearAdditiveMagma / NearAdditiveMagmaWithZero / NearAdditiveGroup constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: NearAdditiveMagma([Fam,] gens) returns the near-additive magma generated by gens (closure under +). NearAdditiveMagmaWithZero returns closure under + and Zero. NearAdditiveGroup returns closure under +, Zero, and AdditiveInverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family Fam can be provided and is required if gens is empty (so the domain family is specified). These are constructors for building the corresponding domains from generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: NearAdditiveMagmaByGenerators / ...ByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: NearAdditiveMagmaByGenerators, NearAdditiveMagmaWithZeroByGenerators, NearAdditiveGroupByGenerators provide underlying operations for creating the respective structures from generator lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used internally as underlying operations for the constructors above.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubnearAdditiveMagma / SubadditiveMagmaNC
rubrics_metrics.description: SubnearAdditiveMagma(D, gens) returns the near-additive magma with parent D generated by gens. SubnearAdditiveMagmaNC does the same but does not check membership of gens in D. Synonyms SubadditiveMagma and SubadditiveMagmaNC exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NC variants to avoid membership checks when you know gens lie in D (faster).

rubrics_metrics.name: SubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero / SubnearAdditiveGroup / NC variants
rubrics_metrics.description: SubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero, SubnearAdditiveGroup and their NC variants return substructures (with zero or with inverses) generated by gens under the appropriate closures, with NC skipping membership checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synonyms SubadditiveMagmaWithZero, SubadditiveGroup etc. exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAdditivelyCommutative
rubrics_metrics.description: IsAdditivelyCommutative(A) is true iff for all a,b in A we have a + b = b + a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous testing for multiplicative commutativity uses IsCommutative.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma / WithZero / Group
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma(A) (and corresponding WithZero and Group variants) return a list of elements whose closure (under the relevant operations) generates A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators list is such that closing under addition (and zero / inverses as appropriate) yields A.

rubrics_metrics.name: AdditiveNeutralElement
rubrics_metrics.description: AdditiveNeutralElement(A) returns the neutral element z of a near-additive magma A satisfying z + a = a = a + z for all a in A, if such exists; otherwise returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A near-additive magma that is not in the magma-with-zero category can still have a neutral element z, but z may not be obtainable using Zero(A) or 0*a.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero
rubrics_metrics.description: TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero(A) returns the additive magma-with-zero whose only element is the zero of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute returns the trivial (single-element) substructure containing only the zero element.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClosureNearAdditiveGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: ClosureNearAdditiveGroup(A, a) or ClosureNearAdditiveGroup(A, B) returns the closure of A with an element a or a near-additive magma B with respect to addition, zero, and additive inverses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to generate smallest near-additive group containing given elements or substructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShowAdditionTable / ShowMultiplicationTable
rubrics_metrics.description: ShowAdditionTable(R) and ShowMultiplicationTable(M) pretty-print the addition or multiplication table of a structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given for GF(4) to illustrate formatted table output.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRing
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRing(R) indicates R is a ring: an additive group and a magma such that addition + and multiplication * are distributive (IsDistributive). Multiplication need not be associative (so non-associative structures like Lie algebras are treated as rings in GAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ring is a broad category: division rings, fields, algebras are rings; check IsDistributive to ensure ring property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring constructor
rubrics_metrics.description: Ring(r, s, ...) returns the smallest ring containing the elements r, s, ...; Ring(coll) returns smallest ring containing elements in coll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If elements don't lie in a common ring an error is raised. Ring differs from DefaultRing in that Ring returns smallest such ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultRing
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultRing(r, s, ...) or DefaultRing(coll) returns a ring that contains the given elements but not necessarily the smallest ring; it returns a 'sensible' default ring for the element types (method-dependent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by various ring functions when no explicit ring is given (e.g., Quotient, IsPrime, Factors, Gcd). Example: DefaultRing(2, E(4)) returns GaussianIntegers (while Ring(2,E(4)) returns <ring with 2 generators>).

rubrics_metrics.name: RingByGenerators / DefaultRingByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: RingByGenerators(C) returns the ring generated by elements of collection C (closure under +, *, additive inverses). DefaultRingByGenerators(coll) returns a default ring containing coll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default form may pick a conventional ambient ring type (e.g., Gaussian integers) rather than the mathematically smallest ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfRing
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfRing(R) returns a list of elements that generate ring R under addition, multiplication, and additive inverses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: R := Ring(2, 1/2); GeneratorsOfRing(R) returns [2, 1/2].

rubrics_metrics.name: Subring / SubringNC
rubrics_metrics.description: Subring(R, gens) returns the subring of R generated by gens (with parent R). SubringNC does not check that gens lie in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NC variant to skip membership checks for performance when safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClosureRing
rubrics_metrics.description: ClosureRing(R, r) or ClosureRing(R, S) returns the ring generated by R together with element r or subring S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to enlarge a ring by adjoining elements; example: ClosureRing(Integers, E(4)) gives a ring-with-one with 2 generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient (ring elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotient([R,] r, s) returns a right quotient q such that r = q * s in ring R (or default ring) if such q exists, otherwise fail. Result may not be unique in rings with zero divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To perform division in the quotient field use the quotient operator '/'. Examples: Quotient(6,3) returns 2; Quotient(2,3) returns fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of left/right/two-sided ideals and their testing
rubrics_metrics.description: A left ideal in ring R is a subring closed under left-multiplication by elements of R; a right ideal closed under right-multiplication; a two-sided ideal closed under both. Whether a ring I is an ideal in R is queried via IsLeftIdeal(R,I), IsRightIdeal(R,I), IsTwoSidedIdeal(R,I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are attributes IsTwoSidedIdealInParent, IsLeftIdealInParent, IsRightIdealInParent stored on the ideal for fast access. Ideals are constructed with LeftIdeal, RightIdeal, TwoSidedIdeal. Many ideal methods rely on linear algebra and are most applicable to ideals in algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: TwoSidedIdeal / LeftIdeal / RightIdeal (constructors)
rubrics_metrics.description: TwoSidedIdeal(R, gens[, "basis"]) (and LeftIdeal, RightIdeal) return the ideal in R generated by gens. If optional "basis" provided, gens are assumed basis vectors (no linear independence checks). Ideal is synonym for TwoSidedIdeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned ideal has LeftActingRingOfIdeal / RightActingRingOfIdeal attributes to access R. Example: I := Ideal(Integers, [2]).

rubrics_metrics.name: NC variants for ideals (TwoSidedIdealNC etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: TwoSidedIdealNC, LeftIdealNC, RightIdealNC behave like their checked counterparts but do not verify that gens lie in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NC variants when generator membership is known and you want to avoid checks for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsTwoSidedIdeal / IsLeftIdeal / IsRightIdeal properties
rubrics_metrics.description: IsTwoSidedIdeal(R, I), IsLeftIdeal(R, I), IsRightIdeal(R, I) test whether I is the respective ideal in R. Attributes IsTwoSidedIdealInParent, IsLeftIdealInParent, IsRightIdealInParent are stored on the ideal when known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example showing Ideal(A, [ Random(A) ]) and IsTwoSidedIdeal(A, I) returning true.

rubrics_metrics.name: TwoSidedIdealByGenerators / LeftIdealByGenerators / RightIdealByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: TwoSidedIdealByGenerators(R, gens) returns the ring generated by gens under addition, multiplication, and left- and right-multiplication by R. LeftIdealByGenerators and RightIdealByGenerators return left- or right- ideals generated similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators and acting rings can be accessed via GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal and LeftActingRingOfIdeal / RightActingRingOfIdeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal / GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal / GeneratorsOfRightIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal(I) (and left/right variants) return lists of generators for the ideal I with respect to actions from left and/or right by the acting rings stored on I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GeneratorsOfIdeal is a synonym for GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal. Example: GeneratorsOfIdeal(I) may return a matrix basis for ideals in matrix algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftActingRingOfIdeal / RightActingRingOfIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftActingRingOfIdeal(I) and RightActingRingOfIdeal(I) return the left and right acting rings of an ideal I, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes indicate from which ring the left or right action is taken when viewing I as a module or ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsLeftIdeal / AsRightIdeal / AsTwoSidedIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: AsLeftIdeal(R, S) returns S viewed as a left ideal of R if S is indeed a left ideal, otherwise fail. Similarly AsRightIdeal and AsTwoSidedIdeal for right and two-sided ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let S be a subring of R; these operations test whether S is an ideal of the specified type and return it cast as such if so. Examples show AsTwoSidedIdeal(B, C) returning an ideal when C is a subalgebra that is a two-sided ideal in B.
